findings.title: HTTP reads and injects extend the idle bound, so a token holder can keep a dead-peer shell and cap slot alive indefinitely
findings.evidence: ADR-030 section 6 ('An accepted inject and a read both update the session's last-activity time'; 'The websocket still has to be open'); src/api/routes/demo_terminal.py:51-60 (idle bound exists because a vanished peer never sends disconnect) and :372-378 (sole reaper); cap at :68
findings.consequence: Polling GET output with wait=10 resets the clock forever; a SIGKILLed browser leaves its shell running and one of six slots occupied until restart; six such sessions block all new terminals. Reintroduces the orphaned-shell defect D06-A finding 2.
findings.minimal_fix: Reads never extend; injects extend only up to an absolute ceiling since the last websocket frame, or drop the extension and document the 300 s reap; rewrite open item 4 accordingly.

findings.title: Stated check order (peer, token, request) and single error shape are not what FastAPI produces; a literal build breaks the contract
findings.evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/scratch/exp.py: malformed JSON without token -> 422 (not 401); text/plain valid JSON with token -> 422 (not 415); bad query -> {"detail":[...]} not {"error":{...}}. ADR section 'The contract phase-wbf-08 builds'.
findings.consequence: Unauthenticated callers can observe 422 before auth; 415 and the error shape need hand-written handling or an app-wide RequestValidationError handler outside wbf-08's declared deliverables; builder must guess.
findings.minimal_fix: Specify raw-body reading and manual JSON/query validation behind an auth dependency, and an explicit precedence order for 403, 401, 404, 415, 413, 422, 409.

findings.title: Token-in-file rationale is false: shells start in the server cwd and can read data/terminal-api-token, the same exposure used to reject the env-var form
findings.evidence: ADR section 3 and alternatives ('readable from inside the sessions it protects ... a file that only the caller reads'); src/demo/factory.py create_adapter(cwd=None) and demo_terminal.py:355 pass no cwd; src/db/connection.py:6 data/ is cwd-relative.
findings.consequence: An agent or process inside any terminal session can cat the token and drive other sessions; the owner would ratify on an incorrect advantage claim.
findings.minimal_fix: Correct the alternative's reasoning to the real differences, and optionally place the file outside the shell's cwd tree or start shells elsewhere.

findings.title: Token file scheme underspecified: creation mode and symlink handling, cwd-relative path, import-time rewrite under tests and multi-process, Windows protection unverified
findings.evidence: ADR section 3 ('generated when the API module is imported', 'rewritten on each server start', 'mode 0600 on POSIX'); verified open(p,'w') on an existing 0644 file keeps 0644; test/test_demo_terminal.py:195-217 reloads src.api per test; ADR states owner machine is Windows and 0600 is best-effort and unrun.
findings.consequence: Pre-existing or symlinked file can leak or redirect the token; tests or --reload/--workers clobber a running server's token causing 401s; no test path override so the builder invents one; the 'other users' benefit is unproven on Windows.
findings.minimal_fix: Require atomic create (unlink, O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW, 0o600), a repo-root-anchored absolute path logged in full, an overridable path parameter for tests, a single-process note, and reclassify the Windows protection as unverified.

findings.title: Buffer and last-activity record exist on first-flag-only launches, contradicting 'additive' and 'browser behaviour unchanged'
findings.evidence: ADR 'Absence with the flag unset' ('they exist but no route reads them'); Consequences; src/api/__init__.py:27 imports demo_terminal under the first flag alone.
findings.consequence: Every rehearsed demo launch retains up to 256 KiB of raw shell output per session in memory for an API that is off, and runs a changed idle loop.
findings.minimal_fix: Create the record only when the second flag is set, or disclose the change in open item 1.

findings.title: Pump and inject behaviours differ from the description: blocked send stalls the buffer, tail after exit can be lost, lock does not cover websocket writes, write OSError gives 500
findings.evidence: demo_terminal.py:243-251 (send_bytes awaited between reads; loop ends on adapter.alive), :383 (unlocked adapter.write), src/demo/posix.py:47-49 (os.write without OSError handling) and :52-61 (read returns b'' on EIO).
findings.consequence: Flaky R17/R18 tests on shell exit and on slow browsers; session_ended race returns 500; blocked executor writes can starve pump reads.
findings.minimal_fix: Document stall coupling, drain to EOF after exit, map write OSError to 409 session_ended, use a dedicated executor or state the lock's limit.

findings.title: Contract gaps a wbf-08 builder must guess: raw body limit, parameter bounds, session_id format, peer edge cases, long-poll wake mechanism
findings.evidence: ADR contract sections for input (4096 bytes applies to decoded input only), output (limit, wait, after bounds), peer check (two literals only; request.client may be None).
findings.consequence: Different builders ship different status codes and edge behaviour; tests cannot be written from the ADR alone.
findings.minimal_fix: Add a short validation table covering these cases and name the wake mechanism.
